answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable bond backed by verifiable work history before it may trade. Creating a thousand hollow identities is cheap, but funding each one with a bond that is slashed on fraud is not: an attacker must risk real capital per identity, and the bond stays locked while reputation accrues, like heat held in basalt long after the fire. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest from fees, so a single ember of genuine activity grows into trusted standing, while mass-produced clones burn their own capital and gain nothing.
